_whatThisIs: ONE TABLE OF REVIEWS AND THE ANSWERS BOTH IMPLEMENTATIONS MUST GIVE.
There are two copies of the Fayr score: src/review/theFayrScore.js, which
answers as somebody types and cannot be a network call per keystroke, and
backend/src/reviews/fayr-score.ts, because the SERVER scores what it stores
and a number the server cannot vouch for is not worth storing. The app never
sends a score; it sends the text.
Two copies of one rule drift. This table is what makes that a failing check
rather than a surprise: src/review/theFayrScore.test.mjs and
backend/src/reviews/fayr-score.spec.ts both run their own implementation
over every row here and assert every field.
WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, said plainly: it is a cross-implementation agreement
check, not a specification of what a good score is. A divergence that touches
no row here would pass. The RULES — that it is sentiment-blind, that distinct
words beat length, that stock phrases drag it down — are asserted properly in
theFayrScore.test.mjs, against reasoning rather than against recorded output.
So: add a row here whenever a word list changes, and never treat a row as
evidence that a score is RIGHT — only that the two sides agree about it.
